text:
leo: quick alert: we rolled condenser9b v1 with INT4 kernels + prefix cache on the docs-summarize route (canary 10%). Seeing a reproducible entity-drop pattern on long-doc slices — named entities missing or replaced.

rachel: Can you drop an example and the perf/econ delta?

leo: Example (sanitized):
```
INPUT: 3.8k token product spec with 6 named entities (company names / product ids)
PROMPT: extract (entities), then summarize
FP16_OUTPUT: Entities: [AcmeCorp, Aero-42X, ...]; Summary: ...
INT4_OUTPUT: Entities: [Acme], Summary: ...  // missing suffixes, some abbreviations expanded incorrectly
```
Traffic: canary=10%, tokens_in ~3800, avg_steps=2 (extract->summarize). p50 latency +5% vs fp16, p95 similar. Unit cost (hosted): fp16 $0.020/request; INT8 $0.011; INT4 $0.0048.

omar: Any regressions flagged by the eval harness?

eval-bot: Automated check: docs-entity-slice failure rate increased from 1.1% to 6.9% on condenser9b.int4 (threshold 2%). Token-alignment metric down 1.6%.

rachel: This smells like quantized attention k/v drift + prefix cache amplification — long prefix means many k/v writes; low-bit accumulators can push small errors that matter for exact entity spans.

nina: For product/GTN: what's the recommended default? We need a 2-line blurb and expected cost savings.

leo: My ops idea: keep INT4 for short-doc single-step summarization, route long-doc multi-step to INT8. Simple token threshold routing: if tokens_in > 3000 or steps >1 -> int8. Pseudoconfig: 
```
policy: route_by_predicate
predicates:
  - if: tokens_in > 3000
    route: condenser9b.int8
  - if: steps > 1
    route: condenser9b.int8
  - else: condenser9b.int4
```
Also propose: disable prefix_cache for condenser9b.int4 entirely until we validate kv-stability.

rachel: Agree. Additionally, add a soft-eval: compute entity_f1 and span-shift delta per-route and set automated rollback if entity_f1 drops >2% AND absolute failure rate >2% over 20m.

omar: Ops checklist for rollout: (1) feature-flag the routing policy; (2) run a 12h A/B smoke with synthetic long-doc traffic; (3) monitor entity_f1, token_alignment, p95 latency, and mem/disk pressure; (4) if rollback trigger fires auto-pin to int8.

leo: I ran a quick simulated traffic run in staging: int4 w/ prefix_cache off reduces entity failures by ~1.8 points but still worse than int8. So disabling cache helps but not enough.

nina: For GTN blurb: can you quantify UX tradeoff?

leo: Draft blurb: "Recommendation: default to INT4 for short, single-step document summarization to capture 2-3x cost reduction; route long documents or multi-step pipelines to INT8 to avoid entity/regression risk. Expected unit-econ delta: INT4 ~60-65% cost savings vs INT8 on high-token requests; estimated UX impact if misrouted: entity omission or minor hallucination risk ~+4-7% on complex slices."

rachel: Also add note: "If customer prefers aggressive cost savings, offer INT4 with explicit opt-in and visibility: per-route entity_f1 and token_alignment dashboards + an SLA exclusion for long-doc pipelines."

omar: I'll prepare the rollout PR for the route + flag. Need a short runbook snippet for SRE with rollback steps and evaluation command-lines.

leo: I'll attach failing examples to the PR and a json patch for the canary to switch tokens>3000 -> int8.

eval-bot: Scheduling 12h A/B smoke: condenser9b.int8 vs condenser9b.int4; slices: docs-entity-slice, long-doc-summary, multi-step-extract.

nina: Thanks team. We'll hold GTN announcement until smoke completes and we have per-route dashboards. Please ping me when green.

leo: Will do. Tagging @omar for rollout window and @rachel for eval thresholds. :rocket:
